title: POC scoping - Horizon Data integration planning
next_steps: Send pilot SOW and pricing (Maya) by 2026-09-13
Share security docs and SOC2 report (Maya) by 2026-09-12
Schedule benchmark run and provide access details (Liam) by 2026-09-14
Customer to provide sample payloads and throughput targets (Daniel) by 2026-09-12
action_items: Maya Patel: draft and send POC statement of work + pricing by 2026-09-13
Liam Chen: circulate benchmark harness, script and sample data links by 2026-09-14
Daniel Ortiz: share example API payloads, expected qps and peak concurrency by 2026-09-12
Rashmi Kapoor: confirm legal/compliance required docs and residency constraints by 2026-09-15
summary: POC scoping for Horizon Data to validate Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDK integration for an internal analytics assistant. Primary goals: confirm success criteria (latency <= 200ms p50 API for short inferences, cost target per 1M tokens), run benchmarks with sample payloads, validate function/tool-calling & structured output for extraction pipelines, and agree on a 6-week pilot timeline.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. we scheduled 50 minutes, is that still good?
[00:04] Sofia (Horizon Data - CTO): yeah that's perfect. we have Rashmi and Daniel here.
[00:07] Rashmi (Head of ML): hi, thanks. excited to kick this off.
[00:09] Liam (Redwood SE): great, i'm Liam from Redwood's solutions engineering team, i'll drive the benchmarks side.
[00:13] Maya: quick agenda — clarify success criteria, walk thru integration points (sdk/openai compatibility), discuss benchmarks and sizing, and agree pilot timeline. sound ok?
[00:20] Daniel: sounds good. just to call out, we run an analytics assistant over our event store, typical prompt lengths 120-400 tokens, but we also have some long context calls up to 4k tokens.
[00:32] Rashmi: and throughput — baseline ~80 qps for short queries, spikes to ~300 qps during business hours.
[00:38] Liam: ok noted. that's helpful. for the POC we usually scope two workloads: short interactive queries and batched longer summarization.
[00:45] Maya: Rashmi, what would success look like for you after the POC?
[00:48] Rashmi: main things: latency targets (p50/p95), cost per 1M tokens — we have a budget cap for experimental infra, and quality — answers must hit our NLU metrics (F1 on entity extraction >= 0.88).
[01:02] Sofia: also data controls — we need VPC or private deployment options and audit logs for queries for compliance.
[01:08] Maya: yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated options exist; for POC we can run hosted endpoints with a dedicated capacity reservation if needed. We'll share SOC2 and the compliance pack.
[01:18] Daniel: can you describe the API compatibility? we have existing integrations built against OpenAI's completions/chat endpoints.
[01:24] Liam: Redwood offers OpenAI-compatible endpoints and an official SDK. most customers swap endpoints with minimal code change. function/tool calling is supported; structured JSON outputs can be validated via our schema enforcement hooks.
[01:36] Daniel: by "OpenAI-compatible" do you mean same request/response shapes and function call semantics?
[01:40] Liam: yes, same shapes for chat completions and function calling. we also extend with streaming and per-token cost breakdowns, but your payloads should work straight away. occasional header names differ but we have migration guides.
[01:50] Rashmi: any gotchas with tokenization differences? we saw subtle differences across models affecting cost.
[01:55] Liam: good question — tokenization can vary by model family. for the POC we'll run our tokenizer against your sample payloads and include adjusted cost estimates in the benchmark.
[02:04] Maya: ok next, benchmarks. Liam, what do you need from Horizon to run a representative test?
[02:08] Liam: sample prompts (realistic user queries), expected concurrency/throughput matrix, and a small validation set for quality checks. ideally a sample of long-context sessions too. we'll provide a harness and instructions.
[02:18] Daniel: we can export a 10k sample of recent queries, anonymized. is that enough?
[02:22] Liam: yes, that's perfect. for the pilot we'll run: 1) 10k short-query synthetic replay at 80 qps, 2) spike test to 300 qps, 3) long-context batch runs with 1-2k token sequences.
[02:35] Rashmi: timeline? we'd like results in ~3 weeks to decide on dedicated capacity.
[02:39] Maya: we typically do a 4-6 week pilot; we can try to compress to 3 if both sides prioritize artifacts and access.
[02:47] Sofia: what does "prioritize" mean — what's blocking?
[02:49] Liam: access to sample payloads and an engineer to unlock keys and network access for the benchmark runner. also approval to run spike tests against your staging environment.
[02:58] Daniel: staging's ok. we need to review safety checks.
[03:00] Maya: we'll share the benchmark checklist and a gasket for network requirements.
[03:04] Rashmi: about structured output — we have an entity extraction pipeline that expects strict JSON with fields id, entity_type, start, end, score. can Redwood enforce that?
[03:13] Liam: yes — function calling + schema enforcement can enforce JSON shapes; we also run a post-validate step in the harness and flag mismatches.
[03:20] Maya: and if the model returns malformed JSON we provide automatic repair attempts and fallbacks to a deterministic extractor if needed.
[03:27] Rashmi: cool. and for tool calling — we want the model to call internal enrichment services securely. is that supported?
[03:33] Liam: supported. we recommend a mediator service pattern where calls go through a vetted gateway; Redwood can proxy or you can manage that gateway. we have examples in the SDK.
[03:41] Daniel: network-wise we need to ensure no sensitive event payloads are logged in hosted trial. is query logging opt-in?
[03:47] Maya: yes; by default logs for hosted are stored for 30 days for debugging but can be turned off or sent to your S3 with KMS. for POCs we can set no-persist mode and provide audit logging only to your bucket.
[03:58] Sofia: what about KMS integration? we need HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest.
[04:02] Maya: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via standard KMS providers; on-prem/private supports HSMs. we'll put the integrations doc in the follow-up.
[04:10] Rashmi: how do you measure cost in the benchmark? tokens + GPU utilization? we want per-1M token estimate plus projected monthly spend at 100k queries per day.
[04:17] Liam: we measure raw token usage, throughput, GPU utilization and estimate cost with our pricing model. we'll include a runbook that projects cost for your actual volume.
[04:24] Daniel: for long context runs we worry about KV cache memory behavior and latency tail. do you simulate steady state with warm caches?
[04:31] Liam: yes, we'll do warm-cache runs and cold-start runs. also measure kv cache hit rates and tail latencies.
[04:36] Rashmi: any docs/examples for SDK integration? languages we use: python backend, node for some microservices.
[04:42] Liam: official SDKs for python and node.js, plus minimal example to swap endpoint with openai-compatible call. we'll share quickstart repo link.
[04:50] Maya: ok let's talk success criteria numbers — Rashmi suggested p50 <= 200ms for short queries. does that align?
[04:56] Rashmi: yes, p95 ideally < 400ms. if you can't hit that with hosted we'll evaluate dedicated capacity.
[05:03] Liam: for short queries that's achievable on optimized instances; we'll include recommended instance types and quantization profiles.
[05:09] Daniel: recommend instances? we run on GCP but open to dedicated hosts/cloud options.
[05:14] Liam: we'll recommend both GCP and AWS instance families; for POC we'll run on our hosted infra but can replicate on customer-reserved GPUs if you want.
[05:23] Sofia: security red flags from our side: data residency in EU for EU customers, SSO integration, and ability to restrict engineers' console access.
[05:31] Maya: we have SSO/SAML, RBAC, and region controls. for the POC we'll give scoped console access and a masked debug view.
[05:39] Rashmi: ok pricing — do you have template pricing for a 6-week pilot that includes a small reserved capacity?
[05:44] Maya: yes we'll send a pilot pricing template; typical pilots run $X–Y depending on reserved vs fully hosted. i'll include options.
[05:50] Daniel: in terms of acceptance criteria, aside from latency and quality, we need exportable logs and a contract for data deletion post-POC.
[05:58] Maya: we'll add a clause in the SOW for data deletion and retention.
[06:02] Liam: operationally for the benchmark we propose these steps: 1) Horizon provides sample payloads and metrics, 2) Redwood runs replay and spike tests, 3) run quality evals against your validation set, 4) share full report and cost projections.
[06:14] Rashmi: makes sense. can we get an initial benchmark within 10 business days after we hand over data?
[06:18] Liam: yes — assuming access and data by 2026-09-12 we can deliver results by 2026-09-24.
[06:24] Maya: i'll follow up with the SOW and security pack by end of week.
[06:28] Sofia: ok last question — do you support function chaining or only single-step function calls?
[06:33] Liam: function chaining patterns are supported in the SDK with orchestrator helpers; for complex pipelines customers often use a mediator service with Redwood for calls.
[06:40] Rashmi: great.
[06:42] Maya: quick recap and next steps: Maya sends SOW + pricing + security docs; Liam shares benchmark harness and quickstart repo; Horizon provides sample payloads and concurrency targets; everyone gathers for a benchmark kickoff call.
[06:55] Daniel: noted. thanks all.
[06:58] Maya: thanks, we'll send calendar invite for the kickoff after the SOW lands.
[07:03] (end)
